motion: Is finite theism preferable to naturalism?

definitions.label: Appeal to authority
definitions.definition: Relying on a person or institution's status as if it settles the argument, especially when the relevant evidence, expertise, or consensus has not been shown.

definitions.label: Argument from ignorance
definitions.definition: Treating a claim as true because it has not been disproved, or false because it has not been proved, rather than supplying positive evidence.

definitions.label: Begging the question
definitions.definition: Assuming, directly or indirectly, the very point that needs to be established, so the conclusion is smuggled into the premises.

definitions.label: Equivocation
definitions.definition: Shifting the meaning of a key word or phrase during the argument, making the reasoning seem stronger than it is.

definitions.label: Red herring
definitions.definition: Diverting attention from the issue under dispute to a related but less relevant point, leaving the original challenge insufficiently answered.

definitions.label: Special pleading
definitions.definition: Applying an exception or different standard to one side of the argument without giving a principled reason for the difference.

definitions.label: Ambiguity effect
definitions.definition: Preferring clearer or more familiar claims over uncertain ones, even when the uncertain option may deserve serious consideration.

definitions.label: Authority bias
definitions.definition: Giving extra weight to a claim because it comes from a perceived authority, sometimes beyond what the evidence itself supports.

definitions.label: Base-rate neglect
definitions.definition: Underweighting general background rates or prior probabilities while focusing too heavily on a vivid specific case or local detail.

definitions.label: Belief bias
definitions.definition: Judging an argument by whether its conclusion feels believable instead of evaluating whether the conclusion follows from the premises.

definitions.label: Confirmation bias
definitions.definition: Seeking, interpreting, or remembering evidence in ways that favor an existing view while discounting contrary information.

definitions.label: Scope neglect
definitions.definition: Failing to adjust judgment in proportion to the scale, number, or magnitude of what is being discussed.

definitions.label: Subjective validation
definitions.definition: Treating a claim as especially accurate or meaningful because it feels personally resonant or confirms one's private experience.

moves.currentDescription: Because horrific evolutionary suffering conflicts with unlimited power joined to perfect goodness, Goff concludes that suffering strongly counts against the traditional all-powerful, all-knowing God.
moves.lockedProposition: Terrible suffering, including the horrific process of natural selection, is powerful evidence against an all-knowing, all-powerful, perfectly good God.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: on the other hand, I also think the terrible suffering we find in the world is powerful evidence against the traditional omniod. All knowing, all powerful, perfectly good. Why would a loving God who can do anything choose to bring us into existence through the horrific process of natural selection, for example? And you know, I wrestled
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff identifies a concrete evidential tension between terrible suffering, especially suffering produced through natural selection, and a creator possessing unlimited power, complete knowledge, and perfect goodness, without inflating the tension into deductive disproof. Principal limitation: The move does not examine whether sufficiently important goods, creaturely independence, or constraints other than power could justify such suffering, and it initially bears against classical theism rather than supporting finite theism over naturalism. Live burden: Goff must show that a precisely power-limited good creator predicts the actual suffering better than both naturalism and competing limited-deity models, without tailoring the limitation solely to observed evil.

moves.currentDescription: Because divine predictions depend on God’s available worlds, values, and choice dispositions, Oppy concludes Goff lacks enough divine psychology to assign this world a favorable likelihood.
moves.lockedProposition: Judging how likely God is to create this world requires insight into divine psychology, including God's available worlds and values, despite God being very different from us.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: amount of insight into divine psychology really. But it's not, you know, it's not clear that that's going to be right if you imagine that God's so very different from us because what matters here is the range of options that are open to God, right? What kinds of worlds, what kinds of values could be imbued with and so on. um that's going to matter when you're trying to work out how likely it is that God would make this world.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy attacks the exact warrant connecting value to prediction by identifying the information a likelihood requires: which worlds God can create, how God ranks their values, and how those rankings guide selection. Principal limitation: The objection establishes underdetermination without demonstrating that reasonable partial knowledge could never support a directional comparison, and it offers no concrete naturalistic likelihood against which Goff’s modest judgment can be measured. Live burden: Oppy must show that uncertainty about divine psychology is large enough to defeat Goff’s claimed advantage rather than merely preventing precise numerical probability.

moves.currentDescription: Because divine purposes explain fine-tuning while divine limitations explain suffering, Goff concludes that one good, power-limited God can jointly accommodate both central data.
moves.lockedProposition: A limited-power God can explain fine-tuning through divine purposes and suffering through divine limitations.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: But actually, you don't you don't have to choose, right? If you go for some kind of theism, something godish, but not the omniod, I think you can account for both data. And what I go for is a god of limited powers, who's made the best universe they can. Um, and we can and so we can explain both. We explain fine-tuning in terms of God's purposes and suffering in terms of God's limitations. Right? So God just can't
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff presents the debate’s clearest motion-level synthesis by assigning fine-tuning to purposive creation and severe suffering to limited divine power, thereby offering one intelligible hypothesis for evidence pulling against both chance and omnipotent theism. Principal limitation: Both explanatory attributes are initially stipulated, and their convenient division of labor does not demonstrate that such a creator exists, has those exact limitations, or predicts the data better than naturalism. Live burden: He must independently motivate divine goodness, purpose, and the relevant power boundary, then show that their combined explanatory gain outweighs the additional commitments and unresolved divine psychology.

moves.currentDescription: Because likelihood depends on selection among available worlds, Oppy concludes that choosing this borderline world from many better alternatives could make its probability under God approximate chance.
moves.lockedProposition: A world's probability under a creator depends on the divine selection procedure; if God chose among many better worlds, this world's likelihood could approximate chance.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: there's lots and lots of worlds God sticks a pin in and out comes this world right and it's just terrible compared to most of the worlds that God could have made it was right down at the bore borderline just barely creatable and everything else was above and it was very like unlikely that you'd get it. Then for all we know it turns out the numbers are about the same. That's the kind of worry
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy sharpens abstract uncertainty into a probability-relevant scenario: if God could choose among many superior worlds through a broad selection procedure, mere compatibility with value would not make this particular world substantially expected. Principal limitation: The pin-selection procedure and abundance of better creatable worlds are hypothetical, so the example defeats an unsupported inference but does not establish that theism’s actual likelihood equals or approaches naturalistic chance. Live burden: Oppy must justify the relevant option space or show that Goff bears the unmet burden of constraining it before claiming evidential advantage.

moves.currentDescription: Because God can choose fundamental structure and constants but cannot intervene afterward, Goff concludes that evolutionary suffering reflects a precise creative limitation rather than indifference.
moves.lockedProposition: God can select a universe's fundamental physical structure and constants but cannot intervene afterward.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: precisely specified. Take physics, take the values of the fundamental constants out that will give you a certain kind of structure. Well, my hypothesis is that God can create a universe with that structure, but can't fiddle thereafter.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff replaces a vague appeal to finite power with an exceptionally clear boundary: God can establish a universe’s initial physical structure but cannot subsequently alter its development, which directly explains divine nonintervention during evolution. Principal limitation: No independent metaphysical or observational reason supports this remarkably specific division between initial creative capacity and later incapacity, making the hypothesis appear calibrated to preserve fine-tuning while absorbing suffering. Live burden: He must justify why this power profile is possible and antecedently credible, explain whether God had better initial structures available, and answer Oppy’s objection that delimiting divine powers also embeds controversial assumptions about possible worlds.

moves.currentDescription: Because specifying which universes God can create also restricts the space of possible worlds, Oppy concludes Goff’s precise power limit carries an independent modal burden.
moves.lockedProposition: Restricting God to this world's structure also delimits what kinds of worlds are possible, rather than merely specifying divine power.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: >> and that's [snorts] not just a assumption I think about God but maybe it is but it also seems to be assumption about what kinds of worlds there could be when especially if you're thinking that any worlds can't be made by God you're going to be you're kind of delimiting the range of possibility there in an interesting way I think
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy reveals that Goff’s suffering solution is not merely a harmless definition of divine power: saying God can create exactly certain structures commits the theory to substantive claims about what alternatives are genuinely possible. Principal limitation: The move identifies this modal burden without providing a rival account of possibility or proving that divine inability must coincide with metaphysical impossibility, leaving the relationship between agent capacity and world possibility somewhat compressed. Live burden: Oppy must explain why the unsupported modal restriction counts more heavily against finite theism than naturalism’s own initial-state commitments.

moves.currentDescription: Because ignorance of future choices would not prevent alternative initial creation, Goff concludes limited foreknowledge cannot explain why a good God required suffering-laden natural selection.
moves.lockedProposition: Limiting divine foreknowledge is insufficient to explain suffering because God could still have created humans without natural selection.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: theists actually but that's not enough because well God still could have made made us without natural selection right that doesn't explain why God chose natural selection so I think this is why I give these limitations on the kind of universe God was able to create to explain for example why natural selection.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff precisely separates two kinds of limitation: inability to know future contingencies does not entail inability to choose a different initial creative process, so Oppy’s neighboring open-theist option does not yet explain evolutionary suffering. Principal limitation: The reply conditionally assumes that the alternative deity possesses access to better initial structures, while Goff has not independently established that his own stronger power restriction is more credible than the epistemic model he rejects. Live burden: He must support the claimed boundary on available creation methods and demonstrate that it predicts the observed evolutionary process rather than merely accommodating it retrospectively.

moves.currentDescription: Because life requires constants within exceptionally narrow ranges, Goff concludes that current physics makes our apparently chance-selected, life-permitting universe demand comparative explanation.
moves.lockedProposition: Fine-tuning requires physical constants to fall within a very narrow life-permitting range, making our universe appear highly improbable by chance according to current physics.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: about the finetuning of physics for life. This is the discovery of recent decades that for life to be possible, certain numbers in physics have to fall in a in a in a very narrow range. So on the face of it, it looks sort of wildly improbable that our universe would get the right numbers for life just by chance. And yet it does. We won the cosmic lottery. At least that's how things look according to our current best physics.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff clearly connects the narrow life-permitting ranges described by current physics to a provisional explanatory demand, carefully presenting apparent improbability rather than claiming that physics already demonstrates divine selection. Principal limitation: The move supplies neither particular constants nor a defensible probability distribution across their possible values, so narrowness alone cannot establish how improbable the observed combination is under naturalism. Live burden: He must convert this initial appearance into a comparative likelihood argument showing that finite theism expects these constants substantially more than naturalism does, while answering necessity and multiverse alternatives.

moves.currentDescription: Because constants fixed in the initial state would be necessary despite remaining unknowable beforehand, Oppy concludes their values need no explanation as chance-selected alternatives.
moves.lockedProposition: If the constants are fixed in the initial state, they are necessary even though their values cannot be known a priori.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: constants are fixed in the initial state, then they turn out to be necessary. And so you have an explanation for um why the values [clears throat] are as they are. And it won't do to say that there's um that somehow or other there's something more that needs explaining here. Right? So our priority couldn't tell what the values are, but if the theory of modality is right, it turns out that they couldn't have been otherwise. It's
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy offers a substantive modal alternative to chance by distinguishing metaphysical necessity from a priori knowability: investigators can initially lack the constants while those constants nevertheless could not have been otherwise. Principal limitation: Locating values in an initial state does not itself establish necessity, and the underlying Aristotelian account of modality is asserted rather than defended, making the conclusion that no further explanation is required too strong. Live burden: Oppy must justify why the actual initial state fixes the genuine possibility space and answer Goff’s claim that necessary truths can still receive epistemic evidential support.

moves.currentDescription: Because an initial cosmic Quran inscription would strongly support Islam, Goff concludes that analogous apparently purposive fine-tuning should likewise provide strong evidence for theism.
moves.lockedProposition: If a Quran inscription in the universe's initial structure would strongly support Islam, then analogous purposive structure in fine-tuning should strongly support theism.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: following argument, right? Premise one, the awesome evidence that I've just described will be strong evidence for Islam. Premise two, if the ev awesome evidence is strong evidence for Islam, then the finetuning is strong evidence for theism. Conclusion, the finetuning is strong evidence for theism. So, I
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff states an explicit premise-and-conclusion structure that uses an intuitively powerful hypothetical inscription to test whether purposive-looking cosmic structure can provide evidence for agency, thereby moving beyond merely noting narrow constants. Principal limitation: An unmistakably semantic religious message differs importantly from life-permitting numerical values, and the move does not defend the bridge transferring evidential force from deliberate linguistic content to a structure compatible with several nonpurposive accounts. Live burden: Goff must identify the shared evidential property, show that it survives Oppy’s modal framework, and establish support for finite theism rather than generic agency or traditional theism.

moves.currentDescription: If both theories permit identical constant ranges and comparable indeterministic fixation, Oppy concludes the observed fine-tuning is equally explained and therefore favors neither worldview.
moves.lockedProposition: If constants become fixed indeterministically and theism and naturalism permit the same range, both explain the result equally and fine-tuning favors neither.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: indeterministic transition from where they haven't been fixed to when they are. And so the kind of interesting question there is what's the range of possibilities in the the case and in the naturalist case. If you if you think there's the same range of possibilities, then we basically this is just a draw. We have [laughter] an equally good explanation on either side. that fine tuning isn't evidence for anything right
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy gives a clear conditional branch for contingent constants: equal ranges and comparable indeterministic selection structures under theism and naturalism would yield equal evidential fit, neutralizing fine-tuning rather than making it evidence for naturalism. Principal limitation: Neither equality of possibility ranges nor equality of probability measures is established, and Goff’s hypothesis specifically adds purposive weighting that may prevent the stipulated symmetry. Live burden: Oppy must defend the antecedent or show why Goff cannot legitimately alter the distribution through value-directed creation, while keeping metaphysical and epistemic comparisons distinct.

moves.currentDescription: Because conditioning on our universe separates its existence from its parameter values, Goff concludes that fine-tuning itself gives no additional support to a multiverse.
moves.lockedProposition: Once the existence of our universe is backgrounded, its fine-tuning does not favor a multiverse; any nearby multiverse support comes from the universe's mere existence.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: And once you do that, we see that that evidence does not favor a multiverse at all. That's what this equation demonstrates. But so so what so what falls out of that I think is that if there's any support for a multiverse in this vicinity, if there's any evidence for a multiverse, it's from the mere existence of our universe. It's just from the mere fact that Bob, our universe exists. There's nothing to do with the finetuning.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff draws a useful evidential distinction between support arising from the mere existence of at least one universe and support arising specifically from that universe’s life-permitting parameter values, preventing an imprecise appeal to multiplicity. Principal limitation: The referenced probability equation and its assumptions are absent from this move, while observer selection, the sampling procedure, and the relevant comparison class remain unstated, so the categorical denial of any fine-tuning support is insufficiently demonstrated. Live burden: He must show under a transparent probabilistic model that conditioning on existence really neutralizes multiverse confirmation without similarly neutralizing his theistic inference.

moves.currentDescription: Because fine-tuning is actual whereas the imagined inscription is absent and impossible on Oppy’s view, he concludes the two cases have different evidential standing.
moves.lockedProposition: Fine-tuning and the proposed inscription have different evidential standing because fine-tuning is actual, whereas the inscription is absent and, on Oppy's view, impossible.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: And I don't think that's true. I think they have a very different standing because we actually have fine-tuning and we don't have the other. And if my view is right, we couldn't have the other. So I don't see how um I I'm not committed to making the same response to the hypothesis about awesome evidence as I am to the actuality of the fine-tuning evidence. They seem different to me.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy identifies a real difference between evidence actually possessed and a counterfactual inscription that his modal theory excludes, appropriately limiting his response to commitments within his own framework. Principal limitation: Actuality versus counterfactuality does not explain why the inscription’s conditional evidential lesson fails, and invoking impossibility presupposes the contested modal theory without answering Goff’s point that necessary truths can still be epistemically confirmed. Live burden: Oppy must articulate a principle showing why the analogy cannot illuminate evidential support despite its impossible antecedent, rather than merely reporting that the cases seem different.

moves.currentDescription: Because life-permitting constants need only be significantly likelier under a value-caring creator than chance, Goff concludes exhaustive knowledge of divine psychology is unnecessary for evidential support.
moves.lockedProposition: Fine-tuning favors theism if life-permitting constants are significantly more expected under a value-caring creator than by chance; exhaustive knowledge of divine psychology is unnecessary.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: it's like all all I all you have to say is it's significantly more expected with if there's if there is a a god who cares about value who created the universe getting the right numbers for to make to allow for the possibility of life intelligent life US sitcoms um that is more likely than on chance right and and I think that's a reasonable judgment uh so you don't have to say I totally understand divine psychology
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff correctly narrows the epistemic requirement: comparative evidence needs a defensible direction and meaningful likelihood difference, not an exhaustive map of every divine attitude, option, or decision procedure. Principal limitation: Calling the inequality reasonable does not establish it, because a creator caring about value might choose among innumerable valuable worlds, rank unfamiliar goods above embodied intelligence, or face restrictions changing the relevant comparison. Live burden: He must demonstrate that modest assumptions about goodness sufficiently constrain divine choice to make these constants significantly more expected, while answering Oppy’s many-better-worlds scenario.

moves.sectionTitle: Simplicity, prior probability, and theory comparison
moves.currentDescription: Because necessary identities remain learnable through evidence, Goff concludes metaphysical necessity does not eliminate Bayesian comparison, which concerns epistemic alternatives and probability.
moves.lockedProposition: Necessary facts can still be assessed evidentially through epistemic alternatives because Bayesian reasoning concerns epistemic rather than metaphysical probability.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: Well this is an identity right? Um the standard view at least is that identities are necessary. So there are no possible worlds in which water is not H2O. But when you know if you were considering the evidence you'd consider worlds in which water is not H2O to evaluate the evidential support. Um so so I think it's it's that that's the kind of it's epistemic probability not metaphysical probability that's
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff’s water-and-H2O example clearly demonstrates that a fact’s metaphysical necessity does not prevent agents from learning it through evidence, sharply exposing the gap between modal necessity and epistemic probability. Principal limitation: The analogy establishes that evidential learning remains possible but does not itself determine prior distributions, likelihoods, or whether fine-tuning favors finite theism once all worldview commitments are included. Live burden: Goff must translate the methodological distinction into a defended comparison of actual hypotheses and answer Oppy’s alternative method based on total-theory simplicity and evidential fit.

moves.sectionTitle: Simplicity, prior probability, and theory comparison
moves.currentDescription: Because Oppy rejects universal Bayesian conditionalization, he concludes complete worldviews should instead be compared by simplicity and their fit with the actual evidence.
moves.lockedProposition: Worldviews should be compared as total theories by simplicity and fit with actual evidence, not solely by Bayesian conditionalization.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: >> But but I'm not a basian. I don't think that we do everything by conditionalization. I agree that if if we were basians I couldn't zero these things out. But what I want to do is to compare the total theories and to think about the this theory comparison in terms of fit with the evidence on the one hand and simplicity on the other. And um I'm interested in fitting the actual evidence. That's what that's what your theory has to be
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy clearly states an alternative method and fairly concedes that Goff’s objection would matter within Bayesianism before proposing total-theory comparison through simplicity and fit with the evidence actually available. Principal limitation: Naming these criteria does not justify rejecting epistemic probability, explain how simplicity and fit interact, or apply either measure sufficiently to demonstrate that naturalism defeats finite theism. Live burden: Oppy must operationalize the criteria, count the respective primitive commitments, and show how naturalism fits fine-tuning, suffering, consciousness, freedom, and value at least as well overall.

moves.sectionTitle: Simplicity, prior probability, and theory comparison
moves.currentDescription: Because intrinsic probability roughly tracks simplicity and both competing views are comparatively economical, Goff concludes simplicity alone does not clearly favor naturalism over his limited God.
moves.lockedProposition: Intrinsic probability tracks simplicity, but both naturalism and Goff's precisely limited deity are comparatively simple theories.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: >> I think I've got a simpler answer. I mean, I think I would just say roughly the same. Um I I you know, I think I judge intrinsic probability roughly on simplicity. And I think both my limited guard and naturalism are both pretty simple. And so um
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff accepts Oppy’s principal criterion and grants that naturalism is genuinely simple, narrowing the disagreement to whether his limited-God hypothesis is similarly economical rather than evading theoretical cost. Principal limitation: The claimed tie is unsupported by any accounting of primitive terms, ontological commitments, divine mentality, moral facts, or the exact power boundary added by finite theism. Live burden: Goff must demonstrate that a purposive finite mind plus physical structure is not substantially more complex than naturalism and that explanatory unification compensates for whatever additional commitments remain.

moves.sectionTitle: Simplicity, prior probability, and theory comparison
moves.currentDescription: Because probability has secure application within science but not straightforwardly across philosophy, Oppy concludes Bayesian reasoning should not govern comparative evaluation of entire worldviews.
moves.lockedProposition: Bayesian probability is appropriate in scientific domains but does not straightforwardly extend to philosophical worldview comparison.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: >> So I think that basinism is probably all the rage in the sciences right there right but the domain in which it's actually appropriate to talk about probability really full stop is limited to the case of science right so I'm not I'm not saying that um you know basian statistics and basian reasoning as we know it in all the sciences is a mistake. I just think that it doesn't extend to things like philosophy.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy carefully preserves Bayesian statistics and reasoning within scientific practice, avoiding an indiscriminate rejection while plainly locating his disagreement in their extension to philosophical total-theory comparison. Principal limitation: The proposed science-philosophy boundary is asserted without a criterion explaining why epistemic uncertainty, conditional support, or disciplined probability judgments cease to apply when theories become metaphysical. Live burden: He must defend the domain restriction, explain how his simplicity-and-fit method handles uncertainty more reliably, and avoid relying on likelihood-like judgments under different terminology.

moves.sectionTitle: Simplicity, prior probability, and theory comparison
moves.currentDescription: Because a cited Bayesian case uses background knowledge for theism’s prior but allegedly ignores it for naturalism’s, Oppy concludes its probability comparison is unfairly asymmetric.
moves.lockedProposition: The psychophysical-harmony paper treats background knowledge asymmetrically by using it for theism's prior while ignoring it for naturalism's prior.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: >> So when they're working out the prior for theism, they insist that [laughter] there's lots of background knowledge that they're allowed to take into account. But when they're working out the prior for naturalism, they just ignore considerations about background knowledge altogether in what they say about it. Right? Now that's not fair. Right?
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy identifies a specific methodological defect rather than merely rejecting Bayesianism wholesale: if background knowledge informs one worldview’s prior while being excluded from the other’s, the resulting comparison is structurally unreliable. Principal limitation: The paper’s procedure is neither quoted nor illustrated in enough detail to verify the alleged asymmetry, and the criticism does not directly engage the full consciousness argument Goff presented in this debate. Live burden: Oppy must document the unequal treatment, consider whether the authors offered a principled reason for it, and explain its consequence for Goff’s own case.

moves.sectionTitle: Simplicity, prior probability, and theory comparison
moves.currentDescription: Because theoretical simplicity improves with fewer primitive undefined terms and fewer ontological commitments, Oppy concludes these measures should favor economical total theories such as naturalism.
moves.lockedProposition: A theory's simplicity depends partly on having fewer primitive undefined terms and making fewer ontological commitments.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: better. The second thing is the fewer primitive undefined terms you've got, the better. That's not entirely independent of the first thing, but it's a separate thing. And the third thing is just how much are you committed to by the theory that is sort of onlogically committed. And those things together are what determine the simplicity of the
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy supplies concrete components of simplicity rather than relying on an undefined aesthetic: theories improve by reducing primitive vocabulary and limiting the entities or structures they fundamentally require. Principal limitation: The criteria are not fully justified, weighted, or applied to the competing worldviews, so the move does not demonstrate that naturalism’s physical primitives are fewer or cheaper than Goff’s divine and physical commitments. Live burden: Oppy must perform the actual comparison and show that naturalism’s economy compensates for any weaker fit concerning fine-tuning, consciousness, freedom, or value.

moves.currentDescription: Because selection directly rewards behavior and sophisticated functioning may occur without experience, Goff concludes that natural selection alone leaves the evolution of inner consciousness unexplained.
moves.lockedProposition: Because natural selection selects behavior and sophisticated behavior could occur without inner life, it is unclear why consciousness evolved.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: Because you know natural selection just cares about behavior. And I think we now know with um complex um AI LLM and complicated robotics, you could have very very sophisticated behavioral functioning without any kind of inner life. So why didn't natural selection just make us complicated survival mechanisms, biological robots without any kind of inner life? Um just
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff isolates a genuinely contrastive question: if adaptive behavior is selection’s direct target and comparable functioning could occur without experience, naturalism must explain why conscious organisms emerged rather than behaviorally adequate nonconscious systems. Principal limitation: Contemporary artificial intelligence and robotics illustrate sophisticated output without establishing the biological or metaphysical possibility of complete nonconscious functional counterparts, so the central alternative remains more intuitive than evidenced. Live burden: Goff must defend the relevant counterpart possibility, distinguish selection on behavior from selection on underlying causal organization, and show that finite theism predicts consciousness rather than merely finding it valuable afterward.

moves.currentDescription: Because phenomenal states are identical with behavior-causing brain states, Oppy concludes identity theory accommodates mental causation without requiring an additional purposive explanation.
moves.lockedProposition: On identity theory, phenomenal states are brain states that causally contribute to behavior, so Oppy sees no independent psychophysical-harmony problem.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: My inclination is to say that I don't see what the problem is here. I'm a kind of oldfashioned smart identity theorist. And I think that um that um phenomenal states just are brain states and phenomenal states play a role in the causation of behavior. And this
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy gives a concise naturalistic account on which phenomenal states are not causally idle additions but the very brain states contributing to behavior, thereby answering concerns about how consciousness can affect action. Principal limitation: Identity theory is asserted rather than defended, and establishing causal relevance does not answer Goff’s contrastive question about why evolution produced conscious brain states instead of functionally equivalent nonconscious mechanisms. Live burden: Oppy must show either that such counterparts are impossible or that contingent evolutionary history explains why the identity-bearing route occurred, rather than treating compatibility as sufficient explanation.

moves.currentDescription: Even granting consciousness aids survival, Goff concludes naturalism must explain why equivalent nonconscious mechanisms—or meaningless experience under panpsychism—could not perform the same adaptive work.
moves.lockedProposition: Even if consciousness aids survival, it remains unclear why nonconscious mechanisms—or, for a panpsychist, meaningless consciousness—could not perform the same functions.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: I'm sure our consciousness and our conscious understand our conceptual understanding in consciousness helps us survive. Great. All I'm saying is non it's not it's far from clear why non-concious mechanisms couldn't have done the same in both cases. Why not if you're not a pans psychist why not non-concious mechanisms instead of conscious? Even if you are a pans psychist why not meaningless consciousness instead of conceptually rich consciousness.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff explicitly concedes that conscious understanding may improve survival, then preserves the deeper contrast by asking why nonconscious mechanisms could not provide the same functions, or why panpsychist experience became conceptually meaningful. Principal limitation: The proposed alternatives are not biologically demonstrated, and functional equivalence may conceal differences in learning, integration, flexibility, or causal organization that make consciousness inseparable from the adaptive mechanism. Live burden: He must substantiate the rival mechanisms, explain what finite theism contributes beyond a creator’s presumed preference for valuable consciousness, and compare that contribution with contingent evolutionary history.

moves.currentDescription: Because organisms wired to avoid pleasure would fail to reproduce, Oppy concludes that this proposed disharmonious psychophysical arrangement would be rapidly eliminated by natural selection.
moves.lockedProposition: Creatures behaviorally wired to avoid pleasure would not procreate and would quickly become extinct, so that disharmonious evolutionary scenario does not cohere.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: uh, it seemed to me that if you're thinking about things that way, then creatures that were wired up that way wouldn't procreate, right? They become extinct within a generation because they would be avoiding actually literally avoiding sources of pleasure. So it didn't seem the story didn't hang together for me in a way that made
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy connects a specified behavioral arrangement to an ordinary evolutionary consequence: systematic avoidance of pleasure-associated reproductive behavior would reduce fitness and quickly remove that lineage, giving selection genuine explanatory work. Principal limitation: The response addresses only one disharmonious design and does not exclude Goff’s broader possibility of a nonconscious mechanism producing exactly the same adaptive behavior, so it targets a narrower alternative than the central challenge. Live burden: Oppy must generalize the evolutionary constraint or explain why functionally equivalent nonconscious organisms are unavailable, rather than showing merely that one maladaptive arrangement fails.

moves.currentDescription: Because libertarian agents benefit from rationally understanding their reasons, Goff concludes that freedom combined with selection motivates conscious understanding as an efficient survival shortcut.
moves.lockedProposition: Libertarian freedom plus natural selection can produce conscious understanding that supports rational responses and serves as a shortcut to survival.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: libertarian free will plus natural selection. Because once there's libertarian free will, natural selection I think has a motivation to give us conscious understanding. Because if we're going to respond rationally, sort of primitive rationality to our conscious understanding, I think that's intuitively plausibly we're going to survive well and plausibly it will be a shortcut to surviving well. So natural
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff offers a positive sequence rather than only identifying a mystery: antecedent libertarian agency makes conscious conceptual understanding adaptively useful because reason-responsive choices can then guide survival efficiently. Principal limitation: The proposal assumes that libertarian freedom exists before sophisticated understanding, that selection can act upon the resulting advantages, and that irreducible freedom is required, yet no evolutionary mechanism or comparison with nonlibertarian cognition supports those assumptions. Live burden: He must explain the origin and heritability of the proposed agency, show why ordinary causal cognition cannot deliver the same shortcut, and connect the mechanism specifically to purposive finite creation.

moves.currentDescription: Because contingent ancestral pressures create path-dependent and eventually irreversible trajectories, Oppy concludes evolutionary history can explain why one workable mechanism emerged instead of another.
moves.lockedProposition: Evolutionary outcomes can depend on contingent ancestral pressures and become irreversible after development proceeds far enough along a particular trajectory.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: another? It just has to do with the particular evolutionary pressures that um our ancestors were under at particular periods in our evolutionary history. Once you've gone far enough down a particular trajectory, there's no like you could there was no going back. There was no developing a photo sensing patch at some later stage. So maybe part of the answer to your question is that it is contingent, right? But in this
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy finally offers the appropriate contrastive form of naturalistic answer: contingent early pressures can place a lineage on one workable developmental path, after which accumulated dependencies make alternative mechanisms inaccessible. Principal limitation: This is a credible general pattern rather than a consciousness-specific history, and no evidence identifies which ancestral events selected phenomenal states or why the relevant path required experience instead of nonconscious functioning. Live burden: Oppy must connect path dependence to the actual evolution of consciousness and conceptual reasoning, showing more than the abstract possibility that some contingent story exists.

moves.currentDescription: Because equivalent adaptive behavior might arise through nonconscious mechanisms, Goff concludes Oppy’s identity and selection accounts still do not explain why consciousness evolved instead.
moves.lockedProposition: If a nonconscious mechanism could perform the same functions, evolutionary usefulness does not explain why consciousness evolved instead.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: Couldn't couldn't something different a non-concious mechanism have done exactly the same stuff? And if it could, then we we haven't explained why we evolved consciousness as opposed to non-concious mechanisms that do the same
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff precisely identifies what Oppy’s replies leave open: proving that consciousness causes useful behavior and that one disharmonious creature would fail does not explain selection of consciousness over every functionally equivalent nonconscious route. Principal limitation: The force of this challenge still depends on the unsupported availability of genuinely equivalent biological mechanisms, which may be impossible if phenomenal identity is necessary to the relevant integrated brain organization. Live burden: Goff must defend that possibility and then show that purposive finite theism explains the selection better, rather than merely preserving an unanswered question for naturalism.

moves.currentDescription: Because ancient consciousness may differ from later socially selected reasoning, Oppy concludes distinctively human conceptual capacities need not share one evolutionary origin with phenomenal experience.
moves.lockedProposition: Distinctively human reasoning may have arisen through social-status pressures and need not be tied to consciousness, which may extend much deeper into the animal kingdom.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: establishing social status by being being the first person to know things became very important. This is all highly speculative. It's a a a theory that I like [clears throat] completely wrong, but there'll be some story like that that's to tell about the kind of distinctive reasoning capacities that we've got. And I don't think that those are necessarily tied to consciousness, which I think goes way way deeper into um the animal
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy usefully separates two explananda that Goff sometimes combines: phenomenal consciousness may extend deeply into animal life, while distinctively human conceptual reasoning could have emerged later through communication and social pressures. Principal limitation: Oppy explicitly describes his favored status-based history as highly speculative and possibly completely wrong, and the distinction does not explain why phenomenal consciousness arose in the first place. Live burden: He must provide evidence for the separate evolutionary trajectories and show how dividing the problem produces explanatory progress rather than relocating the unanswered question.

moves.currentDescription: Because free choices rationally answer reasons during deliberation, Goff concludes that libertarian freedom is a fundamental causal relation expressing primitive rational responsiveness.
moves.lockedProposition: Libertarian freedom involves primitive rational responsiveness to reasons and is, by definition, a fundamental causal relation.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: as involving a sort of primitive rationality. You know, if I'm, I don't know, wrestling over a moral dilemma, I'm I'm whichever option I go for, I it's it's a sort of rational it's a response to reasons for action, whether it's moral considerations or my own desires or something. you're responding rationally to your beliefs and desires. Um, and by definition, I think libertarian free will is a sort of fundamental causal relation, right?
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff grounds his conception of libertarian agency in the familiar experience of deliberating over reasons, desires, and moral considerations, giving an intelligible role to agency rather than treating freedom as arbitrary indeterminacy. Principal limitation: Describing libertarian freedom as a fundamental causal relation largely defines the disputed mechanism into the account and supplies little public warrant that deliberation involves irreducible agent causation rather than complex deterministic or probabilistic processes. Live burden: He must establish that this fundamental relation is coherent, genuinely instantiated, and necessary for rational responsiveness before using its value or evolutionary usefulness as evidence for theism.

moves.currentDescription: Although intelligent life may possess objective value, Oppy concludes that value alone does not establish that God has correspondingly greater reason to create or prioritize it.
moves.lockedProposition: Intelligent life may objectively have value without that fact alone giving God greater reason to care about or create it.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: >> Um so I think the answer to that question is yes. But that that that [clears throat] it's got a certain degree of value doesn't mean that God has more reason to sort of care about it than we have to care about the ants.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy grants Goff’s premise that intelligent life has objective value while carefully denying only the further inference that this value supplies God with a comparatively stronger creative reason, producing a focused and charitable rebuttal. Principal limitation: The distinction blocks entailment but remains thin as an account of divine reasons, since sufficiently weighty objective value could still create a defeasible expectation without being uniquely or decisively important. Live burden: Oppy must show that competing divine reasons or beneficiaries make Goff’s directional likelihood judgment genuinely unreliable, not merely logically avoidable.

moves.currentDescription: Because objective libertarian freedom has great value and suits a good creator’s purposes, Goff concludes its availability is more expected under theism than atheism.
moves.lockedProposition: An objective potential for free will is more expected under theism than atheism because free will has great value and is something a god would create.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: logically entail the existence of God, but if there is that sort of objective potential for free will from the start, I think that's more expected given theism than atheism. Uh, you know, yeah, it could be just there by chance, atheism, but it's it's the kind of thing because it's of great value. It's the kind of thing a god would create. It's more expected given theism than atheism.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff converts his agency proposal into an explicitly comparative claim, carefully distinguishing greater expectation from logical entailment and conceding that valuable freedom could still occur without God. Principal limitation: The inference depends on unargued claims that libertarian freedom is objectively valuable, metaphysically available, and something a radically different creator would prioritize, while it does not distinguish Goff’s finite deity from broader theistic alternatives. Live burden: He must defend the value-to-divine-choice bridge against Oppy’s concern about unknown divine reasons and show that the increased likelihood is substantial enough to offset added theoretical commitments.

moves.currentDescription: Because undergoing a phenomenal state differs epistemically from observing it, Oppy concludes physical identity can coexist with first-person privacy and an observer’s incomplete knowledge.
moves.lockedProposition: Identity theory permits a principled privacy difference because being in a phenomenal state differs from observing it, leaving an observer without some first-person knowledge.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: Another thing though is this. I think that for for our phenomenal states, there's something that it's like to be in them, right? And there's a difference between being in a state and observing the state, right? That will still apply you. You may if if you're not in the state that I'm in then there's something that you don't know about my state. Right. That's that's related to the kind of privacy question as well.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy offers a clean distinction between being in a phenomenal state and externally observing that state, preserving the intuitive privacy of experience without abandoning the identity of phenomenal and brain states. Principal limitation: The experiential distinction is plausible but underdeveloped as an epistemology, and defending privacy compatibility does not explain consciousness’s existence, its qualitative character, or its evolutionary emergence. Live burden: Oppy must show how identity theory accounts for the observer’s missing knowledge and connect that defense to naturalism’s overall explanatory fit rather than merely dissolving a subsidiary objection.

moves.currentDescription: Because divine mentality radically differs from human psychology, Goff concludes God may lack ordinary desires while incorporated moral facts perform an analogous motivational role.
moves.lockedProposition: God is a radically different kind of mind without ordinary beliefs and desires; fundamental moral facts are part of God and play the motivational role desires play in us.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: I'm attracted to the view that God is a mind but a very different kind of mind um that doesn't have beliefs and desires in the way we do. So I mean think about I don't I guess I don't think God has desires. So, so I believe there are uh fundamental moral facts, right? And I guess I think those fundamental moral facts are part of God and they they play the role desires play in us.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff resists a simplistic human projection by explicitly describing God as a radically different kind of mind and attempts to ground purposive goodness in fundamental moral facts rather than ordinary appetites. Principal limitation: The account becomes obscure where moral facts are said to be parts of God that motivate action like desires, because neither their metaphysical incorporation nor their causal role in a belief-and-desire-free mind is explained. Live burden: Goff must make this agency model coherent enough to support predictions about creation and show that its added structure improves explanatory power rather than deepening Oppy’s divine-psychology concern.

moves.sectionTitle: Neighboring theisms, polytheism, and strongest challenges
moves.currentDescription: Because undetermined free choices may lack present truth values, Goff concludes divine foreknowledge could be limited, candidly revising his earlier characterization of God as omniscient.
moves.lockedProposition: Goff is open to God lacking foreknowledge of free choices because no future fact yet exists, thereby qualifying his earlier claim that God is omniscient.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: attracted to the idea that yeah, God doesn't know the future. Um, God doesn't know what we're what we're going to do because there's no fact of the matter as to what we're going to do. Um, I'm not totally sold on that. I haven't thought about it that much, but I'm open to that view. So, actually, I'm contradicting what I said a moment ago that I said God's omniscient. I'm open to God's knowledge being limited in that way.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff directly engages Oppy’s neighboring model, openly acknowledges tension with his earlier omniscience claim, and identifies an intelligible open-future basis on which unknowable free choices would not diminish knowledge of existing facts. Principal limitation: He offers no developed account of future truth, time, or foreknowledge, and openness about competing specifications makes the finite-theist hypothesis less determinate precisely where comparative predictions require clarity. Live burden: Goff must decide which knowledge limitations belong to his model, explain their interaction with libertarian freedom, and show that this flexibility increases explanatory adequacy rather than insulating the theory through optional revisions.

moves.sectionTitle: Neighboring theisms, polytheism, and strongest challenges
moves.currentDescription: Because limited foreknowledge prevents anticipating undetermined outcomes, Oppy concludes process or open theism offers a neighboring account of divine limitation without Goff’s precise power boundary.
moves.lockedProposition: Process theology retains divine goodness and love while allowing that limited foreknowledge prevents God from doing many things.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: >> Approach where you definitely say God's perfectly good and perfectly loving. Um maybe you I mean there's a question about how we're going to define omniscience and omnipotence. Maybe God isn't om's not omnisient rather than not omnipotent. Uh but certainly there are lots of things that God can't do because God doesn't know what's [snorts] coming down the pipe. Right.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy broadens the hypothesis space by distinguishing limitation in knowledge from limitation in power, showing that a perfectly loving God could lack future information and therefore be unable to prevent consequences that cannot yet be foreseen. Principal limitation: The move establishes conceptual availability but supplies no reason to prefer epistemic limitation, and ignorance alone may not explain why an initially creative God selected natural selection rather than a less suffering-intensive process. Live burden: Oppy must show how this neighboring theory pressures Goff’s comparative case or supports naturalism, while addressing Goff’s reply that stronger creative constraints remain necessary.

moves.sectionTitle: Neighboring theisms, polytheism, and strongest challenges
moves.currentDescription: Because perfect goodness entails concern for suffering and help when knowledge and ability permit, Goff concludes divine goodness should extend even to comparatively lesser creatures.
moves.lockedProposition: A perfectly good God would care about suffering, and a knowledgeable being able to help lesser creatures would do so.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: good, you're going to care about our suffering, right? Uh I think, you know, if you're perfectly good, you're going to care about the suffering of ants if they suffer. I guess maybe we don't care about it as much because we're sort of limited in what we can do now finite resources. We got to look after ourselves. But if I was perfectly good and omnisient and I could help the ants, I would do so. Yeah. So, so I think
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff supplies a concrete moral analogy in which a knowledgeable, capable, perfectly good person would assist suffering ants, clarifying why he retains divine goodness and explains nonintervention through limited power instead of diminished concern. Principal limitation: The inference projects ordinary moral judgment onto a radically different divine agent and moves too quickly from concern to intervention without considering competing values, priorities, indirect consequences, or unknown beneficiaries. Live burden: He must show that objective goodness constrains divine action in the proposed way and that the creator’s inability, rather than different reasons, best explains unrelieved suffering.

moves.sectionTitle: Neighboring theisms, polytheism, and strongest challenges
moves.currentDescription: Because objective human value need not imply divine priority, Oppy concludes an unknown higher realm of creatures could receive the creator’s principal concern instead.
moves.lockedProposition: The divine-psychology problem remains unless humans grasp the ethics applying to God, who might instead care primarily about unknown higher creatures.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: we have a kind of perfect grasp on the ethics that would apply to God something like that. Um, so it might so so the the kind of hypothesis that you might imagine is that there is another there is another realm of creatures that we don't know about that stand to us as we stand to the ants and they're the ones that God cares about really really cares about.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy provides a concrete counterpossibility separating objective value from divine priority: humans might be valuable while standing to unknown superior creatures as ants stand to humans, weakening Goff’s prediction about creator attention. Principal limitation: The additional realm is wholly speculative and does not positively support naturalism; its force is limited to showing that Goff’s ethical assumptions do not uniquely determine what God would chiefly value. Live burden: Oppy must explain why this underdetermination is materially serious rather than an unrestricted skeptical possibility and connect it to the total-theory comparison.

moves.sectionTitle: Neighboring theisms, polytheism, and strongest challenges
moves.currentDescription: Because one specified limited God requires fewer independent agents and motives, Goff concludes finite monotheism remains simpler than polytheisms containing multiple morally mixed deities.
moves.lockedProposition: Goff's specified God remains comparatively simple, whereas positing many gods with mixed psychologies would add complexity.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: what I'm trying to do. But it's not it's still quite simple. It's still simpler than physics at least how I'm specifying the uh the constants. It's still pretty damn simple. But I think if you're getting into lots of different gods and then they're a bit good and they're a bit bad and they get crossed sometimes. I think it's just going to get more complicated. But
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff directly compares his view with finite polytheism and plausibly observes that multiplying independent agents with differentiated motives and interactions can increase theoretical complexity relative to a single limited creator. Principal limitation: He offers no common measure for comparing divine simplicity with physical theory, assumes polytheistic gods would possess mixed psychologies, and does not count the complexity introduced by his own precisely tailored power restrictions. Live burden: Goff must specify primitive commitments for each rival and show that finite monotheism’s explanatory gains justify its additions over naturalism as well as polytheism.

moves.sectionTitle: Neighboring theisms, polytheism, and strongest challenges
moves.currentDescription: Because much of Oppy’s fine-tuning response depends on Aristotelian modality, he concludes that justifying that contested conception is the strongest challenge facing his current naturalism.
moves.lockedProposition: The strongest challenge to Oppy's current naturalism is justifying the Aristotelian conception of modality on which much of his account depends.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: my view at the moment. I think that um kind of justifying that kind of aristo Aristotilian conception of modality is a kind of serious challenge because of um lots turns on that for the way that I'm thinking about things at the moment.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Oppy candidly identifies the exact foundation carrying much of his modal response and acknowledges that defending it is a serious challenge, giving readers an unusually informative statement of his own position’s principal vulnerability. Principal limitation: The concession necessarily leaves the missing justification unsupplied, so the necessity-based answer to fine-tuning cannot receive independent support from this move and remains conditional upon a contested framework. Live burden: Oppy must defend the Aristotelian restriction on possibilities or provide a naturalistic fine-tuning response that does not depend upon it.

moves.sectionTitle: Neighboring theisms, polytheism, and strongest challenges
moves.currentDescription: Because physics may revise the fine-tuning datum and probability reasoning may contain technical mistakes, Goff concludes his central case remains empirically and methodologically defeasible.
moves.lockedProposition: Goff's strongest doubts are that future physics may remove the fine-tuning datum and that difficult probability judgments may be mistaken.
moves.completeLockedSourceExcerpt: >> I'm I mean my biggest source of doubt with fine-tuning is the evidence could change. I'm very open to that and so that's a source of doubt. Um, and I suppose you're just always open to, you know, questions of how we make sense of these probabilities. You just got to be open-minded that the difficult technical questions, you might be getting something wrong.
moves.assessmentRationale: Strongest feature: Goff identifies two distinct, genuinely consequential defeaters for his own case: future physical theory could remove the appearance of fine-tuning, and difficult probability judgments could reveal that his evidential comparison is mistaken. Principal limitation: This commendable openness does not resolve the existing concerns about probability measures, divine psychology, or modal assumptions, and it underscores how heavily his motion-level conclusion depends on unsettled evidence and method. Live burden: Goff must show that present evidence is sufficiently robust to support finite theism now while specifying what discoveries would materially reduce that support.

overallBlunders.text: The exact divine power boundary—selecting constants while being unable to intervene afterward—was specified with great clarity but almost no independent metaphysical or observational support, making accommodation do more work than prediction.

The cosmic-inscription analogy transferred evidential force from explicit semantic content to life-permitting constants without adequately defending the shared feature or addressing important differences between messages and numerical parameters.

His accounts of libertarian freedom and divine mentality added obscure fundamental machinery—agent causation and motivational moral facts—without showing that these commitments were coherent, evidenced, or simpler than naturalistic alternatives.

The claim that Bayesian probability belongs in science but not philosophy was largely declared rather than argued, leaving no principled boundary or explanation of how worldview uncertainty should otherwise be represented.

Identity theory answered how consciousness could cause behavior but initially missed Goff’s central question of why conscious rather than functionally equivalent nonconscious organization evolved at all.

Oppy’s necessity-based fine-tuning response depended on an undeveloped Aristotelian modal theory, while his alternative equal-ranges branch stipulated rather than established the symmetry required for an evidential draw.
